CV-6.clinicalNotes:
Since the points Qi Hai (CV-6), Guan Yuan (CV-4), and Shi Men (CV-5) possess functions of tonifying the Yuan Qi, they may be used to treat the syndrome of Yuan Qi collapse due to deficiency.

Compared to Guan Yuan (CV-4) and Shi Men (CV-5), this point is used to promote the circulation of Qi and tonify the Yuan Qi.

combinations.indication: Qi and Yang deficiency, fatigue, urogenital disorders

CV-7.category: Meeting Point of the Conception and Penetrating (Chong) vessels
CV-7.locationClassical: In the lower abdomen, on the anterior midline, 1 cun inferior to the umbilicus.
howToFind: In supine decubitus, locate the point
5 cun above Qi Hai (CV-6), or 1 cun below the umbilicus.
CV-7.anatomy: Linea alba. Innervated by the tenth intercostal nerve.
CV-7.safetyWarning: Deep insertion may penetrate the peritoneal cavity.
CV-7.etymology: Yin (陰), Yin of Yin-Yang; Jiao (交), crossing.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-8.locationClassical: In the center of the umbilicus.
howToFind: 1. Palpate the anatomical landmarks for CV-8 along the Conception Vessel (Ren Mai) meridian.
2. Feel for the characteristic depression or inter-muscular groove at the specified Cun measurement.
3. Verify patient sensation (De Qi — soreness, numbness, distention, or heaviness upon palpation).
CV-8.anatomy: Umbilical scar tissue. Innervated by the tenth intercostal nerve.
CV-8.needling: NEEDLING IS CONTRAINDICATED. This point is treated exclusively with moxibustion (frequently over a layer of salt or a slice of ginger).
actions: Rescues the Yang and restores consciousness
tcmIndications: Collapse of the Yang (profuse cold sweating, imperceptible pulse)
CV-8.etymology: Shen (神), spirit; Que (闕), palace gate. The point is located in the center of the umbilical scar, an important passage for the circulation of Qi and Xue from mother to fetus.
CV-8.clinicalNotes: According to Sun Simiao, every point has a symbolic name with profound meaning. "Shen Que" refers to the entrance through which the Shen and Qi pass and to the place that allows fetal growth. Thus, the point possesses physiological characteristics of a vital source; therefore, it may be used in the treatment of digestive and mental syndromes. It is effective in the treatment of afternoon fever and night sweats due to Yin deficiency, and allergic reactions of various etiologies.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-9.locationClassical: In the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 1 cun superior to the umbilicus.
howToFind: In supine decubitus, locate the point 1 cun above Shen Que (CV-8).
CV-9.anatomy: Linea alba. Innervated by the eighth and ninth intercostal nerves.
CV-9.safetyWarning: Deep insertion may penetrate the peritoneal cavity.
actions: treats edema (separates the clear fluids from the turbid fluids)
CV-9.etymology: Shui (水), water and food; Fen (分), separation. The point is located 1 cun above the umbilicus, corresponding to the small intestine, where water and food are separated into pure and impure parts.
CV-9.clinicalNotes: The small intestine acts in the digestion and absorption of nutrients; therefore, this point may be applied to treat borborygmus, diarrhea, regurgitation, and edema.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-10.category: Meeting Point of the Conception Vessel with the Spleen channel
CV-10.locationClassical: In the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 2 cun superior to the umbilicus.
howToFind: In supine decubitus, locate the point 1 cun above Shui Fen (CV-9), or 2 cun above the center of the umbilicus.
CV-10.anatomy: Linea alba. Innervated by the eighth intercostal nerve.
CV-10.safetyWarning: Deep insertion may penetrate the peritoneal cavity.
CV-10.etymology: Xia (下), lower; Wan (脘), stomach. The point is located in the region corresponding to the lower part of the stomach.
CV-10.clinicalNotes: At the level of this point are the transverse colon, the stomach, and the pancreas; therefore, it is indicated to treat gastrointestinal disorders.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-11.locationClassical: In the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 3 cun superior to the umbilicus.
howToFind: In supine decubitus, locate the point 1 cun above Xia Wan (CV-10), or 3 cun above the center of the umbilicus.
CV-11.anatomy: Linea alba. Innervated by the eighth intercostal nerve.
CV-11.safetyWarning: Deep insertion may penetrate the peritoneal cavity.
CV-11.etymology: Jian (建), harmony; Li (里), inner. The point is located in the epigastric region and assists in the regulation of dysfunctions of the Wei (Stomach) and the Pi (Spleen).
CV-11.clinicalNotes: At the level of this point are the Wei (Stomach), the Gan (Liver), and the Pi (pancreas); therefore, it is indicated to treat diseases of the upper abdomen.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-12.locationClassical: In the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 4 cun superior to the umbilicus (at the midpoint between the umbilicus and the costosternal angle).
howToFind: In supine decubitus, locate the point 1 cun above Jian Li (CV-11), or 4 cun above the center of the umbilicus.
CV-12.anatomy: Linea alba. Innervated by the seventh intercostal nerve.
CV-12.safetyWarning: Deep insertion may penetrate the peritoneal cavity.
actions: resolves Dampness and Phlegm. (Principal point for all digestive disorders)
CV-12.etymology: Zhong (中), middle; Wan (脘), cavity. "Cavity" means the inner part of the stomach. The point is located in the area corresponding to the center of the stomach.
CV-12.clinicalNotes:
Front-Mu point of the Wei (Stomach), effective in treating diseases of the Pi (Spleen) and the Wei (Stomach). It may be used for diseases of the Wei (Stomach) such as pain, vomiting, indigestion, diarrhea, and also for diseases caused by hypofunction of the Wei (Stomach) and Pi (Spleen). The Pi and the Wei correspond to the Earth element, according to the theory of the Five Elements. If the Pi and the Wei fail to perform their normal functions, the Earth (Spleen) generates Metal (Lung) deficiently, and may suggest lung diseases such as asthma, excess mucus, and hemoptysis.

Palpitations, insomnia, dissociative disorder, bipolar disorder, and epilepsy are caused by deficiency in the transformation of Qi and Xue (blood), causing deficiency in nourishing the Xin (Heart) or determining the formation of mucus due to deficiency of the Pi (Spleen), consequently causing internal disturbance in the Zang Fu. The retention of dampness in the Middle Jiao manifests as urticaria and jaundice. The fire of the stomach causes a fetid odor in the nose.

This point may be selected for diseases caused by dysfunction of the Wei (Stomach) or as a result of disharmony between the Pi (Spleen) and the Wei (Stomach).

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-13.category: Meeting Point of the Conception Vessel with the Stomach and Small Intestine channels
CV-13.locationClassical: In the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 5 cun superior to the umbilicus.
howToFind: In supine decubitus, locate the point 1 cun above Zhong Wan (CV-12), or 5 cun above the center of the umbilicus.
CV-13.anatomy: Linea alba. Innervated by the seventh intercostal nerve.
CV-13.safetyWarning: Deep insertion may penetrate the peritoneal cavity or perforate an enlarged liver.
CV-13.etymology: Shang (上), upper; Wan (脘), cavity. The point is located in the region corresponding to the stomach.
CV-13.clinicalNotes: Shang Wan (CV-13) is the meeting point of the Conception Vessel with the Stomach and Small Intestine Meridians, located between Zhong Wan (CV-12) and Ju Que (CV-14). Its central clinical function is to harmonize the Stomach and descend rebellious Qi, with preferential indication for patterns in which Phlegm obstructs the Middle Jiao and produces nausea, hiccups, reflux, and high cardiogastric pain near the xiphoid process (Deadman, A Manual of Acupuncture, 2007, p. 511–513). The Jia Yi Jing additionally records indications for food vomiting, hematemesis, and refractory chest fullness. Common combinations: Shang Wan (CV-13) + Zhong Wan (CV-12) + Zu San Li (ST-36) for high functional dyspepsia with regurgitation; with Nei Guan (PC-6) and Feng Long (ST-40) for nausea with Phlegm and anxiety; and with Ju Que (CV-14) for retrosternal distress of gastric origin (Maciocia, The Foundations of Chinese Medicine, 3rd ed., 2015). It is underused because Zhong Wan (CV-12), the Front-Mu of the Stomach and Hui-Meeting of the Fu organs, concentrates almost all Middle-Jiao indications in modern practice — hence the classical referral. Caution: deep needling may reach the left hepatic lobe in thin patients — keep perpendicular insertion at 0.5–1.0 cun. Frequently paired with Zhong Wan (CV-12) and Ju Que (CV-14) for similar complaints; see details under Zhong Wan (CV-12).

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-14.locationClassical: In the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 6 cun superior to the umbilicus (2 cun inferior to the costosternal angle).
howToFind: In supine decubitus, locate the point 1 cun above Shang Wan (CV-13), or 6 cun above the center of the umbilicus.
CV-14.anatomy: Linea alba. Innervated by the seventh intercostal nerve.
CV-14.safetyWarning: HIGH RISK. Deep perpendicular or superior insertion may perforate the left lobe of the liver or the heart.
actions: descends the rebellious Qi of the Stomach
CV-14.etymology: Ju (巨), great; Que (闕), palace gate. Front-Mu point of the Xin (Heart), it treats disorders of the Shen (mind). It is considered that the Xin (Heart) is a palace, and Ju Que is the gateway for the Qi of the Xin (Heart).
CV-14.clinicalNotes:
The Xin (Heart) controls mental activity and the circulation of the blood. Therefore, the point is indicated to treat cardiopathies and mental disorders.

Located at the level of the stomach and liver, it is frequently used to treat digestive diseases. Disorders of the respiratory system due to failure of the Earth (Spleen) to generate Metal (Lung) or due to ascension of the Qi of the Wei (Stomach) may be treated with this point.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-15.category: Luo-Connecting Point of the Conception Vessel
CV-15.locationClassical: On the anterior midline, 7 cun superior to the umbilicus, just below the xiphoid process.
howToFind: In supine decubitus, locate the point 7 cun above the center of the umbilicus, or 1 cun above Ju Que (CV-14).
CV-15.anatomy: Linea alba, insertion of the rectus abdominis muscle. Innervated by the seventh intercostal nerve.
CV-15.safetyWarning: HIGH RISK. Deep perpendicular or superior insertion may perforate the liver or the heart.
actions: descends the Qi of the Lung and the Stomach
CV-15.etymology: Jiu (鳩), dove; Wei (尾), tail. The point is located below the xiphoid process, which is similar to the tail of a dove.
CV-15.clinicalNotes: Ju Que (CV-14) and Jiu Wei (CV-15) are points recommended for the treatment of epilepsy related to mucus. The function of Jiu Wei (CV-15) is to regulate the Wei (Stomach) and the Pi (Spleen) to remove the mucus, being used to treat symptoms such as neurasthenia, dyspnea, and exhaustion from excessive sexual activity.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-16.locationClassical: On the anterior midline, over the sternum, at the level of the fifth intercostal space (at the costosternal angle).
howToFind: In supine decubitus, locate the point on the lower border of the sternum, on the anterior midline.
CV-16.anatomy: Body of the sternum. Innervated by the anterior cutaneous branch of the sixth intercostal nerve.
CV-16.needling: Transverse (subcutaneous) insertion directed superiorly or inferiorly, 0.3–0.5 cun.
actions: descends the rebellious Qi of the Stomach
CV-16.etymology: Zhong (中), center; Ting (庭), courtyard of the imperial palace. The point is located below Tan Zhong (CV-17), as if it were the courtyard in front of the imperial palace. The Xin (Heart) is the governing organ and lies within the pericardium, like the monarch in his palace.
CV-16.clinicalNotes: The point is located near the Xin (Heart) and may be used to treat diseases and symptoms of the cardiocirculatory system. According to clinical experience, this point is recommended for regulating the flow of Qi of the Wei (Stomach), being indicated to treat vomiting, including in children.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-17.locationClassical: On the anterior midline, over the sternum, at the level of the fourth intercostal space (at the midpoint between the nipples in men).
howToFind: In supine decubitus, locate the point at the intersection between the sternal midline and the intermammillary line in men. In women, the intersection between the sternal midline and the line at the level of the fourth intercostal space is considered.
CV-17.anatomy: Body of the sternum. Innervated by the fourth intercostal nerve.
CV-17.needling: Transverse (subcutaneous) insertion directed superiorly or inferiorly, 0.3–0.5 cun.
actions: Regulates the Qi and unbinds the chest
descends the rebellious Qi of the Lung and the Stomach
benefits the breasts and promotes lactation
CV-17.etymology: Tan (膻), stage; Zhong (中), center. The point is located at the center of the chest as if it were a stage.
CV-17.clinicalNotes:
The lungs control the Qi and respiration; therefore, the point is commonly used in diseases of the respiratory system. Lactation is associated with several Zang Fu. The point acts in the regulation of the Qi, being important to increase lactation.

It is used to treat diseases of the digestive system, symptoms of goiter, syncope, and symptoms of cholera.

Because it is the Front-Mu point of the Xin Bao (Pericardium), Tan Zhong (CV-17) is frequently used to treat diseases of the circulatory system.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-18.locationClassical: On the anterior midline, over the sternum, at the level of the third intercostal space.
howToFind: In supine decubitus or seated, locate the point on the midline of the sternum, at the level of the third intercostal space.
CV-18.anatomy: Body of the sternum. Innervated by the third intercostal nerve.
actions: descends the rebellious Qi of the Lung
CV-18.etymology: Yu (玉), jade; Tang (堂), palace. The point is located at the level of the heart, which, like jade, is precious and considered a palace of jade.
CV-18.clinicalNotes: The point is located anteriorly, in the chest, between the lungs and the breasts. Thus, according to the principle of local action, the point may be used to treat disorders of these areas.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-19.locationClassical: On the anterior midline, over the sternum, at the level of the second intercostal space.
howToFind: In supine decubitus or seated, locate the point on the midline of the sternum, at the level of the second intercostal space.
CV-19.anatomy: Body of the sternum. Innervated by the second intercostal nerve.
actions: descends the rebellious Qi of the Lung
CV-19.etymology: Zi (紫), purple; Gong (宮), palace. Zi Gong is the name of a star and refers to the residence of the Emperor. The point corresponds to the Xin (Heart), the monarch of the organs, hence called Zi Gong.
CV-19.clinicalNotes: Due to its location in the frontal region of the chest, between the breasts and anterior to the lungs and esophagus, it may be applied to treat diseases of these organs.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-20.locationClassical: On the anterior midline, over the sternum, at the level of the first intercostal space.
howToFind: In supine decubitus or seated, locate the point on the midline of the sternum, at the level of the first intercostal space.
CV-20.anatomy: Manubrium of the sternum. Innervated by the first intercostal nerve.
actions: descends the rebellious Qi of the Lung
CV-20.etymology: Hua (華), magnificent; Gai (蓋), umbrella. Hua Gai means that the lung is the cover of the five Zang, and the point treats lung diseases.
CV-20.clinicalNotes: The point is located in the center of the anterior region of the chest, at the level of the lungs and esophagus; therefore, according to the local-action property of the points, it is used to treat diseases of the region.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-21.locationClassical: On the anterior midline, in the center of the manubrium of the sternum, 1 cun inferior to CV-22.
howToFind: In supine decubitus or seated, with the neck in extension, locate the point between the first sternocostal articulation and the midline of the sternum.
CV-21.anatomy: Manubrium of the sternum. Innervated by the supraclavicular nerve.
actions: Descends the rebellious Qi of the Stomach and the Lung
CV-21.etymology: Xuan (璇), rotation; Ji (璣), axis. Xuan Ji is surrounded by stars. The lung is located in the upper part of the five Zang, and the point lies in the center of the upper part, with the property of regulating the Qi of the Fei (Lung).
CV-21.clinicalNotes: Due to its location, namely in the region of the lungs and esophagus, and according to the local-action property, this point has been used to treat dyspepsia since ancient China.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-22.category: Meeting Point of the Conception and Yin Linking (Yin Wei) vessels. Window of Heaven Point
CV-22.locationClassical: On the anterior midline, in the center of the suprasternal fossa.
howToFind: 1. Palpate the anatomical landmarks for CV-22 along the Conception Vessel (Ren Mai) meridian.
2. Feel for the characteristic depression or inter-muscular groove at the specified Cun measurement.
3. Verify patient sensation (De Qi — soreness, numbness, distention, or heaviness upon palpation).
CV-22.anatomy: Sternohyoid and sternothyroid muscles. The trachea lies directly posterior. The aortic arch and the brachiocephalic trunk are deep in relation to the sternum.
CV-22.needling: COMPLEX INSERTION. First, insert perpendicularly 0.2 cun. Then, direct the needle inferiorly along the posterior surface of the sternum (anterior to the trachea) for 0.5–1.0 cun.
CV-22.safetyWarning: HIGH RISK. Strict adherence to the angle of insertion is mandatory. Deep perpendicular insertion will perforate the trachea. Deep inferior insertion at an incorrect angle may perforate the aorta or the brachiocephalic artery.
actions: Descends the rebellious Qi of the Lung
benefits the throat and the voice
tcmIndications: plum-pit Qi (sensation of a lump in the throat)
CV-22.etymology: Tian (天), heaven; Tu (突), chimney. The point is located in the upper region of the trachea, like a chimney for the Qi of the lung.
CV-22.clinicalNotes: The point is located anterior to the trachea and may be used to treat globus hystericus and symptoms of goiter. According to the local-action property, it is an important point for treating diseases of the respiratory system.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-23.category: Meeting Point of the Conception and Yin Linking (Yin Wei) vessels
CV-23.locationClassical: On the anterior midline of the neck, in the depression superior to the hyoid bone.
howToFind: Seated, with the neck in extension, locate the point in the depression above the upper border of the laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple).
CV-23.anatomy: Mylohyoid and geniohyoid muscles. Innervated by branches of the hypoglossal nerve and the glossopharyngeal nerve.
CV-23.needling: Oblique insertion directed superiorly toward the root of the tongue, 0.5–1.0 cun.
tcmIndications: Edema and stiffness of the tongue
CV-23.etymology: Lian (廉), prominence of the throat; Quan (泉), spring. The point is located in the depression on the upper border of the laryngeal prominence.
CV-23.clinicalNotes: The point is located at the root of the tongue. According to the local-action property, the point may be used to treat diseases of the tongue and oropharynx.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

CV-24.category: Meeting Point of the Conception Vessel with the Governing (Du)
CV-24.locationClassical: On the face, in the depression in the center of the mentolabial sulcus (directly below the lower lip).
howToFind: Seated with the neck in extension, locate the point in the depression in the center of the mentolabial sulcus.
Figure
12 — Point of the Ren Mai (neck and face).
Figure
13 — Insertion of the needle at the point Lian Quan.
CV-24.anatomy: Orbicularis oris muscle. Innervated by the mental nerve (branch of the trigeminal nerve) and by the facial nerve.
actions: benefits the face and the mouth
westernIndications: post-stroke rehabilitation for facial motor function
CV-24.etymology: Cheng (承), receiving; Jiang (漿), fluid. Saliva accumulates in this place.
CV-24.clinicalNotes:
1. The point is located below the lips and connects with the Large Intestine Meridian, Hand Yang Ming, and the Stomach Meridian, Foot Yang Ming. These meridians circulate through the upper and lower dental arches, and their tendinous meridians and collaterals reach the face. For this reason, this is the principal point for treating diseases of the head, the face, and the sense organs.

2. The Ren Mai controls the Yin, and the Du Mai controls the Yang of the entire body. As a Crossing Point of the Ren Mai and Du Mai, it promotes the balance between Yin and Yang. Indicated for the treatment of epilepsy, hemiplegia, and infantile convulsion due to imbalance between Yin and Yang.

3. According to the property of treatment along the meridian pathway, this point may be used to treat infantile enuresis and urinary incontinence.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

HP-1.english: HP-1 Point (Prof. Dr. Hong Jin Pai)
HP-1.locationClassical: Seated or in dorsal or lateral recumbency. Located in the sternocleidomastoid region (the cervical region overlying the sternocleidomastoid muscle), on the transverse plane that passes through the midpoint of the posterior third of this muscle.
howToFind: 1. Palpate the anatomical landmarks for HP-1 along the Huatuojiaji Points meridian.
2. Feel for the characteristic depression or inter-muscular groove at the specified Cun measurement.
3. Verify patient sensation (De Qi — soreness, numbness, distention, or heaviness upon palpation).
HP-1.anatomy: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, platysma muscle, superficial layer of the cervical fascia, sternocleidomastoid muscle. Superficial layer: transverse cervical nerve, cervical branch of the facial nerve. Deep layer: internal jugular vein, carotid sinus, branches or tributaries of the superior thyroid artery and vein, branches of the hypoglossal nerve, of the ansa cervicalis, of the accessory nerve (which innervates the sternocleidomastoid muscle), and of the vagus nerve.
HP-1.needling: Perpendicular or oblique insertion according to regional anatomy.
actions: Opens the channel and alleviates pain
westernIndications: Pain in the ipsilateral upper limb
complex regional pain in the upper limb
HP-1.etymology: HP1: Classical nomenclature reflects anatomical topography and therapeutic function.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

HP-2.english: HP-2 Point (Prof. Dr. Hong Jin Pai)
HP-2.locationClassical: Seated or in dorsal recumbency. In the anterior antebrachial region, 3.0 cun distal to the midpoint between Shao Hai (HT-3) and Qu Ze (PC-3).
howToFind: 1. Palpate the anatomical landmarks for HP-2 along the Huatuojiaji Points meridian.
2. Feel for the characteristic depression or inter-muscular groove at the specified Cun measurement.
3. Verify patient sensation (De Qi — soreness, numbness, distention, or heaviness upon palpation).
HP-2.anatomy: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, antebrachial fascia, aponeurosis of the biceps brachii muscle, flexor carpi radialis muscle, palmaris longus muscle; more deeply, the flexor digitorum profundus muscle. Superficial layer: anterior branch of the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, tributaries of the median antebrachial vein and basilic vein. Deep layer: ulnar nerve, ulnar artery and ulnar veins with their branches or tributaries, branch of the median nerve.
HP-2.needling: Perpendicular or oblique insertion according to regional anatomy.
actions: Opens the channel and alleviates pain
westernIndications: Tendinitis of the flexors of the wrist
HP-2.etymology: HP2: Classical nomenclature reflects anatomical topography and therapeutic function.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

HP-3.english: HP-3 Point (Prof. Dr. Hong Jin Pai)
HP-3.locationClassical: Seated or in dorsal recumbency. A pair of points in the anterior antebrachial region, on the same transverse plane as Nei Guan (PC-6): one between the tendon of the flexor carpi radialis muscle and the radius; the other between the tendon of the flexor carpi ulnaris muscle and the ulna.
howToFind: 1. Palpate the anatomical landmarks for HP-3 along the Huatuojiaji Points meridian.
2. Feel for the characteristic depression or inter-muscular groove at the specified Cun measurement.
3. Verify patient sensation (De Qi — soreness, numbness, distention, or heaviness upon palpation).
HP-3.anatomy:
Skin, subcutaneous tissue, antebrachial fascia.

Radial point — between the tendon of the flexor carpi radialis muscle and the tendon of the brachioradialis muscle; more deeply, the radial head of the flexor digitorum superficialis muscle, the flexor pollicis longus muscle, and the pronator quadratus muscle. Superficial layer: cephalic vein, lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve, superficial branches of the radial nerve. Deep layer: radial artery and veins, radial nerve with its branches or tributaries, branch of the median nerve.

Ulnar point — between the tendon of the flexor carpi ulnaris muscle and the ulna, tendon of the flexor digitorum superficialis muscle; more deeply, the tendon of the flexor digitorum profundus muscle and the pronator quadratus muscle. Superficial layer: anterior branch of the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, tributaries of the basilic vein. Deep layer: ulnar artery, ulnar veins, and ulnar nerve with their branches or tributaries, branch of the median nerve.
actions: Opens the channel and alleviates pain
westernIndications: Pain in the palmar flexor muscles of the fingers
HP-3.etymology: HP3: Classical nomenclature reflects anatomical topography and therapeutic function.

combinations.indication: Synergistic reinforcement of channel regulation and targeted pain relief.

HP-4.english: HP-4 Point (Prof. Dr. Hong Jin Pai)
HP-4.locationClassical: In ventral or lateral recumbency. In the gluteal region, 3.0 cun medial to the posterior superior iliac spine, on the transverse plane that passes 3.0 cun inferior to that spine.
